title: Deterministic seed manager + artifact packaging for perf regression reproducibility
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our perf regression suite and load harness runs produce non-deterministic results due to multiple sources of randomness (synthetic corpora seeding, load driver scheduling, and host-level timing jitter). This makes triage of regressions noisy and increases CI flakiness. The existing golden artifact workflow (goldenset comparator) relies on ad-hoc archived snapshots with inconsistent metadata, which complicates rollbacks and bisects.

Goal: Build a small, auditable 'SeedManager' service/library and a lightweight artifact packaging format so every perf/regression run records deterministic seeds, environment fingerprints, and a single artifact bundle that can be re-run locally or on CI to reproduce a failing run. This should be minimally invasive to existing runners and compatible with the Rust loadgen migration and current orchestration.

Scope (what we'll deliver):
- Design and implement a SeedManager library (Rust + thin Python shim) that centralizes RNG seeds for: synthetic corpus selection, scenario-level perturbations, and driver-level client ids.
- SeedManager API: deterministic seed derivation from (commit_hash, scenario_id, run_id, optional user-specified base_seed). Provide stable hashing and versioned seed namespace to allow future changes.
- Integrate SeedManager into the Rust loadgen runner (ENG-131009) and provide a shim that the JS/node runners call during transition.
- Define a small artifact packaging format (tar.gz with manifest.json) that contains: scenario spec snapshot, seed manifest, environment fingerprint (OS, kernel, Docker image id, CPU feature flags), dependency lockfile, and a minimal produced-samples.gz.
- CI integration: add a job that on perf-regression failure uploads the artifact bundle to S3 and attaches a signed manifest to the regression alert. Backfill for last 30 days of flaky failures (best-effort).
- Update goldenset comparator to accept artifact bundles and perform byte-for-byte replay when provided.

Non-goals: full end-to-end hermetic reproducibility of system-level timing (we will document known limits such as scheduler jitter and network variability). This ticket does not change the canonical scoring logic or eval metrics calculations.
acceptance_criteria: SeedManager library available in crates and PyPI shim with semantic version v0.1.0
Rust loadgen uses SeedManager to drive all randomized choices; CI shows decreased variance on stable baselines over 10 runs
Artifact bundle manifest schema documented and sample bundles produced by CI job
On perf regression failure, artifact bundle is uploaded and linked from the alert within 10 minutes
Goldenset comparator can ingest artifact bundles and perform deterministic replay in >90% of test cases (document exceptions)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Consumers don't adopt SeedManager causing mixed seeding in the fleet. Mitigation: provide compatibility shim and hard-coded warnings in old runners; set deprecation window and monitor adoption metric.
Risk: Artifact bundles grow large. Mitigation: enforce strict bundle contents and gzip samples, provide retention TTL on S3 and sampling for full artifacts.
Risk: Security leakage in artifacts (sampled customer data). Mitigation: sanitize samples, default to synthetic corpora, and require manual approval for any customer-derived artifacts.
implementation_plan: 1) API design doc + manifest schema (Aisha) - 2 days
2) SeedManager Rust crate + Python shim (Marco) - 5 days
3) Integrate into Rust loadgen runner and add feature flag for gradual rollout - 3 days
4) CI job + S3 artifact uploader + alert linking (Infra) - 2 days
5) Goldenset comparator ingestion changes and replay harness - 3 days
6) Backfill scripts and monitoring (metrics for variance/adoption) - 2 days
7) Docs + runbook for reproducing artifacts locally - 1 day
rollout_plan: - Start gated rollout with feature flag on non-prod perf runners for 1 week
- Enable on canonical regression job and run 20 trial replays to validate determinism
- Flip default flag for all runners after adoption >80% and variance metric improved
- Add full failure-path alert that archives artifact bundles and notifies on-call
monitoring_and_metrics: - Adoption: percent of regression runs using SeedManager (tagged in run metadata)
- Variance: median absolute deviation of latency p50/p95 across repeated runs
- Artifactization latency: time from failure to uploaded bundle
- Storage: S3 daily ingress for artifact bundles
